title: Rate limit per credential, not per host; the broker passes on a 429 and backs off
description:
## As asked

Repositories: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour) and JKershaw/simple-dispatcher.

**What this is for.** On 8 November, one session crawled all 4,315 issues through the proxy, retrying every time it was refused. That used up Harbour's proxy rate limit for the whole runner host. The limit is 60 requests a minute, counted per IP address (`proxyLimiter` in `routes/proxy.js`). Every session on the host shares one address, so every other session started getting 429s. Two new autopilot runs couldn't even exchange their start-up credential. Each session's local broker (`harbour-token-mcp-server.js`) turned the 429 into a bare "502 could not authorise", so the cause stayed hidden until someone read the server logs. The investigation is on LIN-4377.

**What we want: the textbook approach, kept simple.** John: "Harbour's goal is to be simple code … let's not swing far in the other way."

* **On Harbour's side,** the existing limiter counts requests per credential when a request carries one, and per IP address only when it doesn't. A busy session then slows only itself, and the protection against unauthenticated floods stays exactly as it is. Change the existing limiter's key, not its structure. Adjust the number if it plainly needs it.
* **On the broker's side,** a 429 is passed on as a 429, with when to retry, and the broker waits and retries rather than failing. The runner's log should say what happened, without any token in it.

No new tiers, no new limiters, no new subsystem. If it takes more than a small change on each side, stop and say why.

**Appetite:** small, on purpose. This is the one ticket in the round where John has asked for less, not more.

**Done looks like:** one session making many requests no longer stops other sessions on the same host, and a refused request shows up as what it is.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Implementation Plan

**Implemented as approved, and done.** The full plan, its revisions, the research and the review are preserved in the task snapshots (the latest captured 2026-11-08T12:25:54Z) and in the comment trail.

**What was implemented:**

* **Harbour, [#2363](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2363>) (merge** `2d5d6c2`**).** `proxyLimiter` keeps its place before auth, with the same 60/min budget, window, message and test skip. It keys on `credential:<sha256(bearer)>` once that bearer has authenticated (a capped set of 10,000 hashes, least recently proven dropped first, removed on a 401), and on the client IP otherwise. The runner-kit broker retries its bootstrap exchange only on a 429 with a whole-seconds `Retry-After` of 60 s or less, at most twice. It passes `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-*` through on forwards.
* **simple-dispatcher, [#331](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/331>) (merge** `be6e08b`**).** Its broker follows the same retry rule. A final exchange 429 reaches the agent as a 429 with `Retry-After`, not a 502. Forwards carry the wait headers. It writes token-free log lines.
* **Close-out tidy, [#2369](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2369>) (merge** `3d2046a`**) and [#334](<https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/334>) (merge** `5172d0a`**).** The runner contract's `exchange` and `forward` rows own the brokers' 429 policy, and both brokers are pinned against them. The final exchange 429 is a recorded difference: the kit's `start` fails, while SD answers the agent. The kickoff generators were brought in line with the doc, the limiter JSDoc says it once, and the limiter test uses the shared mock collection.

**Deviation from the plan:** one. The plan deferred contract rows for the broker policy to a follow-up after LIN-4377. At the operator's request they landed here instead (LIN-4386 was cancelled for that reason).

**Verified on production:** on 2026-11-08 at 12:20 UTC, one session on the runner host was refused 429 after its budget ran out. In the same second, another session got 200 with `ratelimit-remaining: 59`.

fits one session

plan-review due: yes

parent.title: Harbour carries the loop (round 1): the hand carries less

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4378 @ 110e35e05

(Harbour `origin/main` 110e35e05; simple-dispatcher `origin/main` cb79e0009.)

**Why it's harder than "change the key"**

1. **The limiter runs before auth, on purpose.** The comment above `proxyLimiter` (`routes/proxy.js:233`) says it sits ahead of `authenticateProxyToken` so that bad requests still count per IP. At that point a `keyGenerator` can only see the *raw* bearer, not a credential that has been checked. Key on that, and a flood that sends a random bearer each time gets a fresh bucket per request and reaches auth. On a miss, auth does two store reads (`validateToken` + `describeRejectionCause`). So "flood protection stays as it is" doesn't happen by itself. This is the one real design decision: hash the bearer for the key, and make sure rejected bearers still use up the IP's budget. Settle it before writing code.

2. **Start-up exchange is covered, but only because of where the token sits.** The broker sends the bootstrap as `Authorization: Bearer` to `POST /api/proxy/token` (`harbour-token-mcp-server.js:101`), so it gets its own bucket. The 429 fires *before* `exchangeBootstrapToken`, so the single-use bootstrap isn't spent. Retry **only** on 429: a timeout or 5xx may come after the bootstrap was consumed.

3. **On the broker side, forwarded 429s already come through as 429.** `forwardProxyRequest` returns the upstream status (`:255`). The bare 502 comes only from a failed *exchange* (`:229`), because `exchangeToken` turns the status into an error string. What's lost on forwards is `Retry-After`/`RateLimit-*`: only `content-type` is copied. The fix is small: copy those headers through, and add a tagged 429 result plus a bounded wait-and-retry in `exchangeToken`/`makeTokenProvider`.

4. **"Pass on a 429" and "wait and retry" pull against each other on data requests.** If the broker retries forwarded 429s, the agent that caused the problem never sees the 429 and its call hangs. I'd suggest retry for the exchange, and pass through with `Retry-After` for data requests. Confirm with John.

5. **"The runner's log" isn't where the broker writes.** The broker is a stdio MCP server that Claude Code spawns (`harnesses.js:357`). Its `console.error` goes to Claude Code's MCP log, not the dispatcher's. This is the part most likely to grow past "small". Agree up front that token-free broker stderr is enough.

**What's underneath this.** The real cause is a session crawling 4,315 issues one by one while ignoring refusals. Per-credential keying limits the damage on Harbour's side, but N sessions × 60/min still go through one workspace's upstream Linear credential. That's the next shared limit. It's out of scope, but say so, so this ticket isn't read as having fixed it.

**What I'd do first:** write a limiter test (it skips when `NODE_ENV=test`, so it needs its own setup) showing two bearers from one IP getting separate budgets, *and* garbage bearers from one IP still hitting 429 after 60. Keep 60/min: one request a second per session is plenty.

## Survey global: LIN-4378 @ 110e35e05 (LinearViewer) · cb79e0009 (simple-dispatcher)

**Where it lands.** In Harbour, the change goes into one `rateLimit({...})` (`routes/proxy.js:237`), mounted as `proxyLimiter, authenticateProxyToken` on every consumer route across 14 `routes/proxy-*.js` files. This part of the code is tidy and has been getting tidier: route groups have been split out, and the limiter is passed in rather than declared again. The pattern this task needs is already 45 lines below: `defaultCopyTokenCreationLimiter` keys on `account:…`, falling back to `ipKeyGenerator(req.ip)`. Copy that rather than inventing a new one. On the broker side, the change goes into `forwardProxyRequest` in `harbour-token-mcp-server.js`. That file is self-contained (Node `http` only) and has barely changed since LIN-1375.

**What the obvious way would do**
- **It breaks the "stays exactly as it is" promise.** The limiter runs *before* auth on purpose (`proxy.js:233-236`). When the key is worked out, the bearer is still just a string someone sent. If you key on it, a client can rotate made-up bearers and get a fresh 60/min for each one, while every fake bearer still costs two store lookups (`validateToken` and `describeRejectionCause`). `POST /api/proxy/token` has the same problem: bootstraps are single-use, so every exchange lands in its own bucket. Someone should accept or rule out that trade-off on purpose, so a reviewer doesn't find it by surprise. Either way, key on `sha256(bearer)`, never on the raw token.
- **No test would notice.** Because of `skip: () => NODE_ENV === 'test'`, no test ever reaches the key. Export the key function as a pure function and unit-test it. That's a few lines.
- **Docs that would go stale:** `docs/proxy-integration.md:17` ("per IP"), `docs/executive-summary.md:203`, the agent-facing catalog `lib/proxy-instructions.js:1208,1261`, the comment at `proxy.js:233`, `proxy-flight-companion.js:57`, and 14 JSDoc strings saying "Per-IP rate limiter middleware".
- **The broker already passes a forwarded 429 through as a 429.** But `createBrokerServer` writes only `Content-Type`, so `Retry-After` gets dropped. The bare 502 comes only from the **exchange** path (`exchangeToken` → bare string → generic 502), and two tests pin it (`test/harbour-token-mcp-server.test.js:244`).
- **Harbour sends several kinds of 429:**
  - the limiter's, with a `Retry-After` header of 60s or less
  - free-tier and run-limit refusals, with `retryAfter` in the body, possibly a day away
  - upstream provider 429s

  A broker that waits out *any* 429 would park a session for hours, or send a write again. Retry only when a `Retry-After` header is present, under a small cap, for a bounded number of attempts. `lib/providers/jira/client.js:20-60` already spells out that policy. Copy its shape.
- **"The runner's log" isn't on this path.** Claude Code starts the broker via `--mcp-config` (`harnesses.js:356`), so the broker's stderr goes to Claude Code's MCP log, not to SD's oplog. A token-free `console.error('[harbour-broker] 429 … retrying in Ns')` is honest, but it won't land in the runner's log. Say which log was meant.
- **There is a second copy of the broker.** `LinearViewer/lib/runner-kit/broker.mjs` is the person-run twin. It already forwards `retry-after`, but it turns an exchange 429 into `bootstrap exchange failed: HTTP 429`. Fixing only SD's broker leaves the two drifting apart.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:**
- the limiter keyed on a hash of the credential
- a pure test of the key function
- the doc strings above
- the broker passing `Retry-After` through and answering an exchange 429 with a 429
- a bounded retry that only fires when the header is present
- the same few lines in `runner-kit/broker.mjs`

**Better still, but not this task's:** the incident is a symptom. A session that needs all 4,315 issues has no bulk read, so it pages one request at a time and retries blindly. Per-credential limits contain the damage, but they don't give that session a better route. Also, the three kinds of 429 share no machine-readable `code`, so no client can tell them apart without guessing.

## Size of the move (the person's call)

Small, on purpose. John's words on this one: "Harbour's goal is to be simple code… let's not swing far in the other way." He asked whether this is the textbook approach. Use the standard approach for a limiter shared by many clients behind one address, and say in the pull request what that is.

**What the move is.** One busy session should use up its own budget, not everyone's. An agent that hits the limit should be told so plainly and back off, rather than be shown a bare 502.

- **Harbour's limiter keeps its place and its 60 a minute,** but each credential gets its own budget, and a made-up credential can't buy a fresh one. The Surveys found the catch here.
- **An agent over its limit sees a 429 with its wait time, not a 502, and backs off.** Fix it in both brokers: the runner's, and the person-run copy in Harbour's runner kit.
- **Make what was said true:** the "per IP" wording in the docs, the agent-facing instructions and the comments.

Token-free broker stderr is enough logging, even though it lands in Claude Code's MCP log rather than the runner's.

**Not this ticket, but say so in the pull request:** a session that needs every issue has no bulk read, so it crawls. The kinds of 429 share no code that lets a client tell them apart. And many sessions still share one workspace's upstream credential. These are the next limits after this one. Leave them for a person to size.

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself, and record why. Raise a ruling only for John's calls: how big a move is, what's spent, removing a step, the order of work, and authority.

**Done when** two sessions on one host each get their own budget, made-up credentials from one address are still refused, an agent over its limit sees a 429 with its wait time, and a start-up exchange that hits the limit recovers on its own. A test shows each of these, and the limiter code ends no bigger than today's, smaller if it can be.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The plan is sound: its premises match the code at LinearViewer `110e35e0` and simple-dispatcher `cb79e00`, and each witness exercises what it claims to protect.

**How it meets what was asked.** As asked: *"the existing limiter counts requests per credential when a request carries one, and per IP address only when it doesn't … the protection against unauthenticated floods stays exactly as it is."* The plan narrows "carries one" to "carries a credential that has already authenticated". That narrowing is the only way to keep the second half of the same sentence true, because a key built from an unverified bearer gives every rotated junk bearer a fresh bucket and lets it through to the two store reads. John's size record (10:02) already settles it: "a made-up credential can't buy a fresh one". *"A 429 is passed on as a 429, with when to retry, and the broker waits and retries"*: the broker retries the exchange and passes forwarded 429s through, which is the split John's record describes. *"No new tiers, no new limiters"*: the plan keeps one limiter with one changed key, and a capped set of hashes beside it. Nothing is cut.

**On the brief's open question** (first requests and exchanges are still charged to the address): this does not need a ruling. After the change, the address budget pays only for exchanges, each credential's first request, junk bearers, and the first request per token after a Harbour restart. That is about 2 requests per session start, so roughly 30 session starts a minute per host before contention. A crawling session no longer touches that budget, because once it has authenticated, every request it makes, including the ones that get refused, counts against its own credential. If startup contention happens anyway, the new exchange retry absorbs it, which is Done-when 4. The incident cannot recur in this form.

#### What I checked (all hold)

- **Harbour placement and keying.** `proxyLimiter` (`routes/proxy.js:237`) is module scope and runs before `authenticateProxyToken` (`:541`, inside the factory, so it can write to a module-scope set). Every mount in the 14 `routes/proxy-*.js` files is `proxyLimiter, authenticateProxyToken`. `POST /api/proxy/token` (`routes/proxy-token-exchange.js:38`) is `proxyLimiter` alone, and a bootstrap is never added to the proven set (`validateToken` refuses `kind === 'bootstrap'`). So exchanges always fall back to the address, as the plan says. `ipKeyGenerator` is already imported and used by `defaultCopyTokenCreationLimiter` (`:287-289`), and that is the pattern to copy.
- **The limiter block is 60 lines today** (`:232-291`), as the plan says.
- **Headers.** express-rate-limit 8.2.1 with `standardHeaders: true` (draft-6) sends `RateLimit-Limit`, `-Remaining`, `-Reset` and `-Policy`, and sets `Retry-After` on every 429 (`dist/index.mjs:907-908`, the seconds to window reset, ≤ 60). So the broker's rule "retry only on a seconds `Retry-After` ≤ 60" always matches a limiter 429 and never a free-tier refusal, whose wait is in the body.
- **SD broker.** The bare 502 comes from the generic catch around `getWorkingToken()` (`harbour-token-mcp-server.js:229`). `createBrokerServer` writes only `Content-Type` (`:285`). Forwards already pass the status through (`:255`). The plan's change set matches this.
- **runner-kit broker.** `exchangeBootstrap` throws `HTTP ${status}` (`broker.mjs:297`). `FORWARDED_RESPONSE_HEADERS` already includes `retry-after` (`:83`), and `reply` logs method, pathname and status (`:445`).
- **Witness scaffolding exists.** `tests/unit/lin-2944-p3-default-copy-token-limit.test.js` flips `NODE_ENV` the way the plan describes (`:47-48, :167-170`). `server.js:1192` sets `trust proxy` to 1, so address isolation through `X-Forwarded-For` is available. Both broker test files exist.
- **Doc line references** in `docs/proxy-integration.md` (17, 2877, 2963, 2978), `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md:139` and `docs/executive-summary.md:203` are correct. 14 files contain "Per-IP rate limiter middleware".
- **Staleness.** Neither repo has a commit since the ticket was filed. The heads equal the plan's baselines.

#### Notes for the builder (none blocking)

1. **The census test will fail until you classify the new set.** `tests/unit/key-state-census.test.js` scans for module-scope `const NAME = new Set|Map(` in `routes/`, and an unlisted one fails the suite. Add `routes/proxy.js::<name>` to `tests/fixtures/key-state-census.json` as `global-only` under the existing `rate-limiters` exception. Then reword that exception in `lib/key-state-holders.js:131`, which says the stores are "keyed by client IP". That sentence becomes false, so it is part of this change's wording sweep.
2. **Three more stale per-IP statements about `proxyLimiter`** sit outside the plan's list but inside its own description of the behaviour:
   - `routes/proxy-reads.js:4` ("the per-IP limiter");
   - `routes/proxy-rulings.js:185-187` ("`proxyLimiter`, which is per-IP and shared across every proxy endpoint, so N agents on N addresses…");
   - `routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js:133`. Check this one: it is about the token-creation limiter and may still be true.

   The plan's `grep -rln "Per-IP rate limiter middleware"` sweep will not catch any of these. Use `grep -rn -i "per[- ]ip" routes lib` and judge each hit. Leave `routes/dispatch.js`, `routes/email-auth.js` and `routes/task-mode.js` alone: those limiters stay per IP.
3. **`docs/executive-summary.md:203`** says "all public endpoints have per-IP throttling". Reword it so it stays true of the others: the proxy is per credential with an IP fallback, and the rest stay per IP. Don't swap it wholesale.
4. **The worst-case exchange wait can exceed a Bash command timeout.** Two waits of up to 60 s each is 120 s plus request time, which is just over Claude Code's default 120 s Bash timeout for an agent whose first call triggers the exchange. In practice the first wait clears a fixed window, so a second wait is rare. Either cap the total wait (for example, stop retrying once the cumulative wait would pass about 90 s) or say in the PR that the worst case is about 2 minutes. Your call; it changes no witness.
5. **runner-kit has no exchange cache.** `startBroker` exchanges once at startup and throws (`broker.mjs:483-486`). The plan's line "the cached failed exchange is still cleared" applies to SD's `makeTokenProvider` only, so don't add a cache to the kit. Retry inside `exchangeBootstrap` or around the `startBroker` call, with an injected sleep. `startBroker` currently injects `now` and `fetchImpl` but not a sleep.
6. **runner-kit's forwarded-429 log line has no wait.** `reply` logs `METHOD path status`. If you want the kit to match SD's "429 and the wait" line, add the `retry-after` value to that one log call when the status is 429. Otherwise say in the PR that the kit logs status only. B5 passes either way.
7. **Getting the terminal 429 out of SD's generic catch.** `makeTokenProvider` throws `new Error(result.error)` and `forwardProxyRequest` turns any throw into the 502. Carry `status` and `retryAfter` on the tagged result and the thrown error, and branch on `status === 429` in the catch. Keep the 502 body unchanged for every other failure (B4 pins it). Keep the retry inside the shared `inflight` promise so concurrent agent calls wait on one exchange, not several.
8. **Fitting the 60-line budget is tight.** The memory plus the key adds about 12-13 lines. Folding the shared options saves about 4-5, and the placement comment now has more to explain. If the block will not fit without rewriting the two LIN-2944 comments (`:254-258`, `:268-279`), shortening them is fine, because they restate the token-creation limiters and do not change behaviour. Do not move the memory out of the block to hit the number. The plan already commits to reporting both counts.
9. **Removing on rejection should mean the 401 branch only.** The 503 store-failure branch (`:625-629`) is not a rejection and should leave the set alone. Add on success after `result` is truthy. H2 and H3 already cover a wrong placement.
10. **Expected side effect, worth one PR line:** the runner's own long-lived token, which polls `/api/proxy/runner/*`, also moves to its own budget instead of sharing the host address with its sessions. That is the same intended behaviour.

No question for the person. Send to `implementation` with these notes.

## Implementation: two PRs, CI green on both

- **Harbour:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2363 (`f7d1923e`). It changes the limiter key, the runner-kit broker, wording and the area note. CI: `CI success` passed (unit, 4 E2E shards, secret scan).
- **simple-dispatcher:** https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/331 (`07f48e3`). It changes SD's broker. CI: `unit tests` passed.

The two PRs are independent and name each other.

**Harbour.** `proxyLimiter` keeps its place before auth, with the same window, budget, message and test skip. Only its key changes: it is `credential:<sha256(bearer)>` once that bearer has authenticated, and `ipKeyGenerator(req.ip)` otherwise. `authenticateProxyToken` records the hash on success and removes it on a 401. A 503 leaves the record alone. The record is a module-scope `Set` of hashes, capped at 10k. Junk, bootstrap and revoked bearers stay on the IP budget. The limiter block is still 60 lines total; executable lines went from 28 to 42. `provenCredentials` is registered in the key-state census.

**Brokers (both).** The exchange is retried only on a 429 whose `Retry-After` is a whole number of seconds, 60 or less, at most twice. Each wait writes one token-free log line. When retries run out, the result is a 429, not a 502: SD answers the agent with 429 and `Retry-After`, and the kit throws an error naming HTTP 429 and the wait. A 5xx, a timeout or a forward is never retried. `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-*` now reach the agent, and each 429 sent back to the agent is logged with its wait.

**Witnesses.** H1–H3 run the real route chain. B1–B5 are mirrored in both repos. I watched each new test fail against `main`. Mutations turned red the cases that pass on `main` anyway (B4, the junk half of H2), and also "key on any bearer" and "don't remove on 401". Local suites: Harbour unit 24,335/24,335 pass; SD 4,280 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.

**Engineering choices, with reasons:**
- **Open question on the wait cap:** I kept two waits of up to 60 s and did not add a cumulative cap. The worst case is about 2 minutes, which is stated in both PRs. This keeps the same simple policy in both brokers, and an agent whose curl times out just joins the same in-flight exchange.
- **The 14th "Per-IP rate limiter middleware" JSDoc,** in `routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js`, is left as it is. It describes `proxyTokenCreationLimiter`, which is still per IP.
- **The area-note entry is short,** because `runs-and-dispatch.md` was 104 bytes under the guard's cap.

**Follow-ups named, no tickets filed:**
- broker rows in the contract table, after LIN-4377;
- no bulk issue read;
- no machine-readable code that tells the kinds of 429 apart;
- one upstream workspace credential shared by every session;
- the limiter store is still per process.

**Cuts to As asked:** none.

### Leftovers

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2363 at head `26006bd6b5a6a421321f0449786cb892cace54f0`, CI success (unit, 4 E2E shards, secret scan). Companion: https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/331 at head `c47b2ed584e38db95ddedf329c51d7541d69206a`, unit tests pass.

- **tidied:** a lesson in `docs/areas/agent-api.md`. `proxyLimiter` runs before auth, so its key trusts only a bearer that auth has already proved. A limiter test must drive the real route chain with `NODE_ENV` set to something other than `test`.
- **tidied:** a lesson in SD's `docs/areas/launch-and-harnesses.md`. The broker retries only its own exchange, and only on a 429 with a `Retry-After` of 60 s or less. It mirrors the runner-kit broker, so change both. This lesson is about the runner-kit broker too, but it went in SD's note because Harbour's `runs-and-dispatch.md` has only 10 bytes left under its cap.
- **for close-out:** contract rows for the shared exchange-retry and forwarded-429 policy in `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` and SD's byte copy, so the drift is caught by a test instead of by prose. File as a follow-up blocked by LIN-4377, which is reworking that table now. It is not a Waiting note: the plan already named it a follow-up, and it spans both repos.
- **nothing else:**
  - No copy left beside a new owner, no old path, and no Waiting entry settled or made untrue.
  - The remaining "per IP" mentions describe limiters that really are still per IP: token creation and the dispatch limiters. The latter is already noted under Waiting.
  - The four "next limits" (bulk read, 429 codes, shared upstream credential, per-process store) are for a person to size. They are not leftovers of this change's code.

## Review — LIN-4378

Reviewed head `26006bd6b5a6a421321f0449786cb892cace54f0` (LinearViewer [#2363](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2363)) and head `c47b2ed584e38db95ddedf329c51d7541d69206a` (simple-dispatcher [#331](https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/331)). Both PRs are open, MERGEABLE and CLEAN.

CI: green on both heads. Harbour: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success. SD: unit tests. I also merged the current LinearViewer `origin/main` (`d294a190e`, which has moved since base `110e35e0`) into the PR head locally. It merged cleanly, and the limiter, broker, census and LIN-2944 P3 tests pass on the merged tree (97/97). SD `origin/main` has not moved.

### Scope against the plan
What changed on disk matches the plan and the plan-review notes:
- Harbour: the `proxyLimiter` key, the bounded `provenCredentials` set, `noteCredential` in `authenticateProxyToken`, the wording sweep, a census entry plus the `key-state-holders.js` rewording, the runner-kit broker, and area notes.
- SD: the broker, `module-map.md`, and the area lesson.

Nothing goes beyond the plan's places. The limiter block, from `// Rate limiters` to the end of `defaultCopyTokenCreationLimiter`, is 60 lines, the same as before. No new limiter, tier or subsystem was added.

### Regression check
- `git log` on `routes/proxy.js`, `lib/runner-kit/broker.mjs` and `harbour-token-mcp-server.js` shows nothing this change re-opens.
- The LIN-1375 / LIN-1502 / LIN-1948 broker hardening is intact. The token appears only on the outgoing Authorization header, binary bodies are still passed through as a Buffer, and the write opt-in is untouched.
- LIN-3699 still holds: a store fault gives a 503 and does **not** call `noteCredential`, because the call sits after `validateToken` returns and inside the `try`.
- LIN-2944 P3's limiter changed only by having its options folded together, and its test still passes.

### Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Harbour: key always `ipKeyGenerator` (the old behaviour) | H1, H2, H3 red |
| Harbour: key on any bearer's hash (drop the `provenCredentials.has` check) | H2 red (junk gets fresh buckets), H1 and H3 red too |
| Harbour: don't remove the hash on a 401 | only H3 red |
| Kit: `exchangeRetryWait` always null | B1, B3, B5 red |
| Kit: retry any non-ok status | B4 red |
| Kit: drop `ratelimit-*` from forwarded headers | B5 red |
| Kit: no cap on attempts | B3 red |
| SD: `exchangeRetryWait` always null | B1 (and the concurrent-share case), B3 red |
| SD: an exchange 429 goes back to the generic 502 | B2 ×3, B3 red |
